ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (Articles L.561-1 et seq.), Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD5), and Décret n° 2017-924 du 6 mai 2017 relatif au registre des bénéficiaires effectifs

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority in country of origin
Competent authority in country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, EU, and French domestic sanctions screening per AMF and ACPR guidelines; full UBO identification, verification, and beneficial ownership disclosure

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French language only; Latin alphabet with standard French orthographic rules; diacritics permitted where required by French language conventions
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying public service, monopoly, or utility functions
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Administrative appeal to the President of the Tribunal de Commerce within two months of rejection; subsequent judicial review available before the Tribunal Administratif

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for administrative and registered office purposes provided a genuine address is maintained for tax residency, commercial substance, and regulatory compliance; virtual or mail-only addresses generally accepted but subject to tax authority scrutiny
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (typically under 10% for routine SAS incorporations absent red flags or tax audits)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code, Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 and R.123-1 et seq.; Civil Code provisions on contracts and company formation also apply. The SAS is governed primarily by its articles of association, subject to mandatory statutory rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent commercial court registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce) for the registered office, with formalities submitted through the national Guichet unique operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI). The legal entity is registered in the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) and, where commercially applicable, the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic declaration of creation of a legal entity (formalités de création) submitted through the Guichet unique, supported by the signed SAS articles of association and prescribed corporate, identity, beneficial-owner, premises, and publication evidence.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital applies to an SAS. Capital may be fixed at EUR 1 or another amount stated in the articles. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid upon incorporation, with the balance payable within five years of registration. Cash capital is deposited into a blocked account with a bank, notary, or authorized deposit institution, which issues a certificate of deposit. Contributions in kind generally require an auditor's report unless the statutory exemption conditions are satisfied. The stated fee is an approximate USD conversion of the commercial registration charge and excludes legal-publication, beneficial-owner, professional, banking, and advisory costs.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned, being the duly appointed President and/or members of the governing body of [Company Name] SAS, resolve that: (1) the Company accepts and approves the subscriptions for the shares specified in the incorporation documents and acknowledges receipt of the required paid-up cash capital; (2) the registered office is established at [full French address]; (3) [name] is appointed President for the term and under the conditions set out in the articles; (4) [names] are appointed, if applicable, as Directeur Général(s); and (5) the President is authorized to complete all filing, publication, banking, tax, and registry formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm Corporate Structure and Reserve the Business Name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique for name and formation formalities; Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle for trademark searches
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the SAS form, shareholders, share allocation, President, optional Directeur Général, registered office, business objects, accounting period, and beneficial owners. Conduct corporate-name and trademark clearance. Obtain written consent for any domiciliation or registered-office service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is unavailable or misleading, amend the name and articles before filing. If a domiciliation provider rejects the application, obtain alternative premises evidence or a compliant domiciliation contract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Execute the SAS Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private corporate counsel, shareholders, and, where required, a French notary or regulated professional
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare French-language articles specifying the name, form, registered office, term, corporate purpose, capital, share classes, transfer restrictions, governance powers, decision rules, financial year, and dissolution provisions. Execute the articles by all shareholders. Use bilingual or translated documents where foreign shareholders require them, while maintaining a French legally operative version.
required_dossiers: Auditor's report for in-kind contributions, unless legally exempt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure omissions by adopting corrected articles and obtaining replacement signatures. Where an in-kind contribution valuation is defective, appoint or replace the contribution auditor and re-execute the relevant documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Cash Capital and Obtain the Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank, notary, or other legally authorized capital-deposit institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital account in the company's formation name. Submit the signed articles, shareholder subscription schedule, identity and address evidence, beneficial-owner information, and source-of-funds documentation. Transfer at least 50% of subscribed cash capital and obtain the certificate of deposit. The temporary account is released after registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to bank KYC or source-of-funds queries with certified corporate and ownership documents. If the bank declines onboarding, use another eligible institution or a French notary and preserve the audit trail of the capital transfer.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An authorized French legal-announcements publication (journal d'annonces légales) in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the prescribed formation notice containing the company name, SAS form, capital, registered office, corporate purpose summary, duration, President, and registration details where available. Pay the regulated publication charge and retain the publication certificate or attestation.
required_dossiers: Signed articles or approved statutory particulars
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any rejected or defective notice through the publication provider and obtain a new attestation. If the notice contains a material error, publish a corrective notice before or promptly after registry submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the Creation Formality Through the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique electronic portal, with review by the competent commercial court registry and relevant tax or social authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the electronic creation form, upload the signed articles, capital-deposit certificate, publication attestation, registered-office evidence, officer declarations, identity documents, and beneficial-owner filing. Digitally sign and pay the applicable charges. Select the business activities accurately, including online B2B marketplace operation and any warehousing activity.
required_dossiers: Foreign corporate shareholder documents with required legalization or translation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Monitor the portal status and respond within the stated deadline to any registry query. Upload corrected or missing documents, pay any additional charge, and resubmit the formal completeness package. If rejected, obtain the written reason, cure the defect, and file an amended formality; a judicial or administrative challenge may be considered where legally available.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Post-Registration Governance and Tax Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique, French tax administration, social authorities, commercial bank, and applicable professional advisers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the SIREN, SIRET, RCS extract, and updated RNE data. Convert the temporary bank account into the operating account, issue share certificates or maintain the statutory share register as appropriate, establish accounting records, confirm VAT and corporate-tax registrations, and document the first shareholder and board or President decisions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct registry, tax, banking, or social-registration discrepancies through the relevant portal or authority. Record all amendments in the statutory books and adopt shareholder or President resolutions where the correction affects corporate governance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ordinary electronic B2B marketplace operation without manufacturing, regulated goods, or an industrial installation. If the company operates a warehouse or other potentially classified installation, the relevant authority is the Prefecture of the department, supported by the Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general manufacturing or industrial operating permit is required for a standard B2B electronic marketplace. The company must comply with French e-commerce, consumer, commercial, tax, data-protection, product-safety, and distance-selling requirements. A warehouse may require an Installation Classée pour la Protection de l'Environnement (ICPE) declaration, registration, or authorization depending on its activities and thresholds.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition; applicable regional environmental authority, including the Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) and the competent environmental assessment authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for ordinary digital marketplace activities with no industrial installation, material emissions, or environmental works. A warehouse or logistics site must be screened against ICPE and environmental-assessment thresholds on a site-specific basis.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No sector-specific industrial wastewater or VOC threshold is triggered by the digital marketplace activity alone. Any facility must comply with applicable Water Act requirements, municipal sewer conditions, air-emission rules, hazardous-material controls, waste-traceability duties, and ICPE permit conditions. Hazardous and non-hazardous waste must be segregated, stored safely, transferred to authorized operators, and documented.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No special industrial clearance is required for a purely office-based marketplace. The operator must maintain workplace health and safety documentation, emergency procedures, fire-risk controls, evacuation arrangements, and required fire equipment. A leased or operated warehouse requires landlord and local fire-safety compliance, appropriate inspections, structural and storage-load verification, electrical and fire-system checks, and any applicable occupational-health assessment. Public-access premises may also require établissement recevant du public (ERP) compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – official taxpayer portal: impots.gouv.fr; business registration portal: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For foreign entities, mandatory French VAT registration is handled by the competent Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) via form CERFA n° 10643*04 / foreign-company VAT application, submitted through the DGFiP foreign taxpayer unit (Pôle Etranger). Non-EU entities must appoint a tax representative in France unless an EU VAT number is already held; required documents include constitutional documents, power of attorney, identity evidence, proof of foreign registration, and anticipated French business description. Upon complete filing the entity receives an intra-community VAT identification number (FR-NNN…) and, where applicable, a SIREN/SIRET for fixed establishments; for designated cross-border e-commerce sellers, simplified registration via the One-Stop-Shop (OSS) non-established registration interface on impots.gouv.fr is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – a French Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS) is irrebuttably treated as a separate taxable entity subject to impôt sur les sociétés (IS) at the standard corporate rate; no check-the-box pass-through election exists. Territorial_Scope: French corporate income tax applies only to profits attributable to a French permanent establishment or, absent PE, to French-source revenues; no metropolitan France Tax_Exempt_Zone status applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in France. Available elections include: (i) option for French tax consolidation under the régime de l'intégration fiscale (Article 223 A ff. CGI) by a parent holding 95% of a French subsidiary; (ii) application of parent-subsidiary participation exemption (régime mère-fille) with 95% dividend exemption upon making the necessary election; (iii) election to apply worldwide taxation (régime mondial) for foreign permanent establishments under Article 209-II CGI; (iv) for partnerships and similar transparent vehicles, opt-in to corporate income tax under Article 206/239; and (v) anti-hybrid mismatch notifications / neutrality elections under Articles 212, 212-bis CGI as implementing ATAD.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT – Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA), governed by Articles 256 to 310 CGI
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Domestic small-business franchise thresholds: EUR 91,900 for supplies of goods and EUR 36,800 for supplies of services per calendar year (slightly higher reduced-reality thresholds apply); foreign established persons have no franchise exemption and must register from the first taxable French transaction; distance-selling / OSS cross-border threshold for EU arrivals of goods is EUR 10,000; certain B2B marketplace facilitation rules require VAT registration irrespective of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Domestic B2B e-invoicing is mandatory phased from 1 September 2026 (large enterprises) and 1 September 2027 (SMEs), with structured data (UBL/CII/FACTUR-X) transmitted to the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or an accredited private plateform; B2C transactions require e-reporting through PPF; no real-time continuous fiscal transaction clearance for retail VAT exists as of the current date, but imports and exports must be electronically declared through the DGFiP/Douane DELTA framework; goods sold via marketplaces may trigger customs and e-commerce import VAT clearance obligations on the marketplace as deemed VAT collector.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (exonération) applies to the export of movable tangible goods physically dispatched or transported out of the European Union by or on behalf of an established French VAT-taxable person; eligibility requires actual exit from the EU, a bona fide commercial sale or stock transfer, and the exporter to hold proof of dispatch within 90 days of delivery/availability; export of services is generally subject to the B2B place-of-supply rule and is outside French VAT when the customer is established outside the EU, provided the services are not physically linked to French immovable property; zero-rating is denied for goods merely placed in bonded or customs warehouse arrangements without subsequent export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Déclaration d'Exportation) validated through DELTA-XI / ESL
Transport document: Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR note
Commercial invoice reflecting the exported goods and incoterms
Customs authorisation / exit confirmation (acquit of exit)
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT bank credit proof evidencing receipt of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The French tax administration under Article 272, 283, 257 and 268 CGI audits export substantiation during statutory limitation period (3 years, extended to 6 years for concealment); unjustified or fraudulent zero-rating triggers or re-invoices VAT at 20% plus late payment interest of 0.20% per month, penalties of 40% for deliberate misconduct ('mauvaise foi') or 80% for abuse/defraudation, and possible criminal fines and imprisonment; marketplace operators acting as deemed VAT collectors face joint and several liability for uncollected import VAT where export evidence is falsified or missing.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), acting within the Eurosystem, with the French Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority (ACPR) and the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) overseeing foreign-exchange policy and balance-of-payments statistics.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible in both current and capital account transactions. There are no French foreign-exchange controls, no prior authorisations for investment or repatriation, and no restrictions on payments or transfers between residents and non-residents under the EU Treaty free movement of capital. Profit remittance is not subject to FX hurdles, but dividend distributions to non-French shareholders may trigger French withholding tax at the statutory 25% rate, potentially reduced under tax treaties or exempt under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive. Banks will require proof of distributable reserves, a director's resolution, beneficial-owner declaration, and applicable tax forms for the remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no statutory provision requiring the surrender or mandatory conversion of export proceeds. Export receivables may be retained in foreign-currency accounts, converted at market rates, or used directly for external commercial payments. There is no fixed repatriation timeline and no minimum conversion ratio. French banks must, however, declare cross-border transaction flows to Banque de France for balance-of-payments and monetary statistics, and all transactions remain subject to EU sanctions screening.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High for operational payment accounts, but Low for regulated capital escrow or statutory deposit functions. EEA-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) may passport their services into France and can support corporate treasury accounts, local IBANs, and payment flow automation for a B2B marketplace. Offshore EMIs without an EEA passport and without ACPR registration are not compliant and should not be used for SAS treasury. EMIs cannot grant credit, cannot create money, and are not substitute for a full credit institution when letters of credit, import financing, or large uncertain FX settlements are needed.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose an absolute face-to-face mandate for bank onboarding if compliant electronic identity verification under eIDAS and French AML/CFT rules is used. However, major Tier-1 banks in practice require at least one in-person meeting or approved video-KYC interview of the legal representatives and ultimate beneficial owners, especially when the SAS has non-French directors or complex cross-border ownership. Remote opening is feasible with a licensed fintech/EMI or through a fully digital banking process, but the onboarding committee normally retains discretion to demand physical attendance for high-risk jurisdictions or unusual capital injection structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multi-layer offshore shareholding with opaque intermediate holding companies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete legal ownership chart from ultimate natural persons to FR_SAS; certificate of incorporation and registry extract for each intermediate entity; annual financial statements or tax returns proving economic substance; French beneficial-owner declaration (Déclaration de bénéficiaire effectif); notarised subscription or transfer deeds; explanation of any nominee or fiduciary arrangement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or beneficial owners resident in a high-risk or tax-cooperative-review jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passport and proof of residential address of each individual; official tax-residence certificate; source-of-wealth document; regulated-bank reference letter covering the previous three years; professional qualification and business-history summary; details of the underlying commercial purpose in France.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent cash-flow pattern versus declared B2B marketplace activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or management financial statements of FR_SAS; ERP journal and order-management records; platform seller/supplier contracts; monthly marketplace settlement reports; shipping and customs documents (SAD/ECS); VAT returns; bank statement reconciliation of all incoming and outgoing commercial payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Person (PEP) or adverse-media profile on director, shareholder, or beneficial owner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence questionnaire; PEP status declaration and explanation; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds report covering the twelve months before account opening; independent professional letters of reference; results of media and sanctions screening; undertaking to maintain enhanced monitoring and provide annual updates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export-control and sanctions exposure in the B2B product portfolio
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Denied-party screening reports for all counterparties; harmonised-system tariff classification of traded goods; French customs export licences or EU general export authorisation memos; end-user/end-use certificates; corporate sanctions compliance policy; transaction-level escalation log and risk-assessment matrix covering embargoed destinations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for an inbound euro equity contribution from a non-French shareholder is a SWIFT MT103 credit to the FR_SAS EUR IBAN, or a SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001.001.09) if the shareholder is located in the EEA. The payment narrative field must clearly state 'CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION / INCREASE OF CAPITAL' and include the SAS corporate name and SIREN number. The sending bank should use an ISO 20022 purpose code of 'EQUI' (equity purchase) or 'INVS' (investment) if its system permits; the French receiving bank will map the transaction to Banque de France balance-of-payments statistical category for foreign direct investment in equity. Verification package: notarised capital-increase resolution, updated K-bis, shareholder board resolution, written payment instruction from the subscriber, proof of the subscriber's identity and source of funds, and pro-forma compliance with Banque de France BOP reporting requirements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlement within the SEPA zone, use SEPA Credit Transfer (pain.001.001.09) with unique end-to-end reference and an ISO purpose code such as 'SUPP' or 'TRAD'. For non-EEA or foreign-currency disbursements, use SWIFT MT103 with UETR and clear beneficiary bank details; for documentary trade, issue an irrevocable commercial letter of credit by SWIFT MT700 under UCP600, receive confirmations by MT710, and settle drawings via MT752/MT103/MT910. French customs duties and VAT on imports are discharged separately through the DGFiP TVS electronic payment system integrated with the DAU customs declaration.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, and EUR/GBP forward contracts (plain-vanilla FX forwards) with maturities matching the underlying B2B trade receivable or payable exposure

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only where the target currency lacks a deliverable interbank market or where the beneficiary settlement structure legally prevents physical delivery, and strictly for genuine hedging of booked exposure
Cross-currency swaps (fixed/floating or fixed/fixed) to hedge foreign-currency assets, liabilities, or contracted cash flows into euro
Plain-vanilla FX options and put/call collars purchased or structured with an authorised French or EEA credit institution for conditional economic hedging

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, and notes) together with proof of shareholders' approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre National des Entreprises via the Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the fiscal year-end; filing must occur within one month after shareholders' approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to €1,500; compulsory dissolution may be sought by the Registry after two consecutive years of non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (Déclaration de Bénéficiaires Effectifs - DBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre National des Entreprises / Greffe via the Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted concurrently with the annual accounts filing; any subsequent change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to €7,500 for legal persons and possible Registry injunction requiring filing under penalty

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Minutes of the annual ordinary general meeting approving annual accounts and approving any dividend distribution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate record; not filed externally unless a DBE update is triggered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Held and minuted within six months of the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct financial sanction from the Registry, but late approval delays annual accounts filing and exposes the company to Registry penalties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Déclaration de résultats n°2065) and annexes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) - Service des Impôts des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Third working day after 1 May of the following fiscal year; for fiscal years shorter than 12 months, due three months from the closing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of net tax due plus late-payment interest of 0.20% per month applied to unpaid corporate income tax

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit (commissaire aux comptes) if at least two of three thresholds are exceeded: balance-sheet total > €4,000,000; turnover > €8,000,000; average number of employees > 50. Appointment is also mandatory for certain SAS structures with control relationships over other entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual annual accounts prepared under French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général, ANC règlement n°2014-03); consolidated annual accounts, if applicable, prepared under IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The beneficial-owner declaration must be reconfirmed by the legal representative at each annual accounts filing. Any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be filed with the Registre National des Entreprises within 30 days. There is no separate stand-alone annual UBO renewal outside the annual filing cycle.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $4,000–$12,000 per annum for a small B2B marketplace SAS
